requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`. I found no gaps.

**Explicit-checkpoint backend (Bedrock).**
- **Checkpoints on every request.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a Claude model against a mock Converse server and checks both captured requests. Each `system` array has exactly two entries: the system text, then `{"cachePoint":{"type":"default"}}`. The last content block of the last message is the checkpoint. A whole-body count finds exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences, so there are no extras. The second request has three messages and includes a reasoning turn, so the end-of-last-message checkpoint is also checked after a multi-turn exchange.
- **No change to content.** The same test reruns with `fixture-uncached-model`. That run has no `cachePoint` at all. After the helper `without_cache_points` strips the checkpoint blocks, every cached request equals the matching uncached request. This is a strong check that checkpoints change nothing else, including tools and messages.
- **Only when the model supports caching.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` calls `bedrock_caches`. It returns true for Claude and Nova model ids and for a Claude inference-profile ARN. It returns false for Llama and for an unknown model. The CLI test confirms the unknown model gets no checkpoints.
- **Unit-level non-mutation.** The same unit test checks that `place_cache_checkpoints` sets only `options.cache`. It compares the serialized request with an expected request that differs only in that option. It also covers a request whose history has a reasoning turn.

**OpenAI.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` covers this part.
- **No checkpoint blocks.** `assert_no_checkpoints` recursively rejects `cachePoint`, `cache_control`, and `cache_point`/`cache_checkpoint` type blocks in every request body.
- **Unchanged prompt and tools.** The test asserts that `instructions` and `tools` are identical across the two requests of one conversation.
- **Ordered replay.** The second request's `input` begins with the first request's `input` verbatim. It then adds the `function_call` and `function_call_output` items for call id `read`, so prior content is replayed in its original order.

**Delegated and out-of-scope.** Prompt sameness across assessments of one kind belongs to the cited `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts`. The task says not to reassess that requirement. Cache reuse across assessments is a consequence of that requirement together with the checkpoint placement tested here. It is not a separate behavior to test.

Each test carries a `{test}` reference to the subject, so there are no marking gaps. The acknowledgments list is empty, and no gaps need acknowledging.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
test-adequacy requirement, structural requirement, example, citation review, site
review, and a verifier of each of those. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
